source_caption:
The "Behind the Cabin" sequence in The Empty Man (2020) is uniquely nightmarish because it weaponizes sudden scale and cosmic inevitability. Instead of a typical jump scare, the protagonist stumbles upon a massive cult of hundreds of people swaying in perfect, rhythmic synchronization around a towering bonfire. The scene transitions instantly from a quiet, isolated investigation in the woods to an overwhelming manifestation of a shared madness. What makes it deeply terrifying is the cultists' eerie, trance-like indifference to the protagonist; when they suddenly turn and chase him, it feels less like an attack by individuals and more like being hunted by a single, monolithic, and unstoppable hive-mind organism.

source_details.title: The Empty Man
source_details.synopsis: The Empty Man is a 2020 supernatural horror film directed, written, and co-edited by David Prior in his feature directorial debut, based on Cullen Bunn and Vanesa R. Del Rey's graphic novel The Empty Man published by Boom! Studios. Starring James Badge Dale and Marin Ireland, it follows an ex-cop who, upon an investigation into a missing girl, discovers a secret cult. Originally filmed in August 2017 as an international co-production between the United States, South Africa, and United Kingdom, the film received poor scores at test screenings and distributor 20th Century Fox lost faith in its commercial prospects.
